title: Council Post: Make Sure Your Building Stays Investible In The Future
text:
Michelle Galvani, CEO, sonKsuru, Patent Pending QuantumSmart™ Cybersecurity: Quantum Safe, Quantum Secure, Quantum Resistant, Quantum Proof.
The future of business is connected, adaptive, dynamic and immersive. Increasingly, there is a growing importance on buildings that are digitally empowered. In a world where remote work and global teams have become the new norm, building owners need to create spaces that cater to the needs of the modern workforce.
Digitally empowered buildings offer a wealth of advanced technologies and amenities, boosting productivity and collaboration while driving significant returns on investment (ROI). By embracing technology and incorporating it into your building, you can better increase its value and provide an enhanced tenant experience.
Connected Infrastructure For Enhanced Efficiency And Collaboration
A connected infrastructure can help enable seamless communication between global offices, remote workers and in-office workers. High-speed internet, reliable connectivity and smart building systems can help improve efficiency and teamwork, helping businesses attract top-tier talent and fostering a productive work environment.
Connectivity And 6G
A building's connectivity is a critical factor for retaining and attracting tenants. Ensuring that your building has robust and reliable internet access and is 6G-ready can give it an imperative competitive edge in the market.
Digital Signage And Wayfinding
Digital signage and wayfinding solutions can help your building stand out and provide a more user-friendly experience for tenants. Equipping your building with interactive directories, digital room reservation systems and real-time occupancy updates improves the tenant experience.
Cybersecurity
As buildings become more digitally connected, they also become more vulnerable to cyberattacks. Ensuring the building has robust AI, ML and self-healing cybersecurity measures in place will signal to tenants and their workforce that their safety and privacy are a top priority for owners and property managers.
Adaptive Workspaces For Employee Satisfaction And Retention
Adaptive workspaces in digitally empowered buildings that cater to various working styles and needs are another critical factor for business leaders. Flexible work areas inside and outside, ergonomic furniture and smart access control systems can contribute to increased job satisfaction, improved morale and higher employee retention rates. These factors can translate into a more productive and profitable workforce.
Productivity Per Square Foot
Buildings that offer coworking memberships with a mix of private offices, open work areas and comfortable meeting rooms can accommodate the diverse requirements of global teams, remote workers and in-office employees. Supplying a next-gen technology infrastructure through all spaces combined with composable physical amenities across a portfolio of properties supporting work-from-anywhere can increase productivity per square foot for business leaders and drive occupancy for building owners.
Competitive Advantage
Leaders in digitally empowered buildings have the opportunity to gain a competitive advantage over their peers in more traditional spaces. The advanced technologies, workspace memberships and amenities offered can help businesses attract top talent, foster innovation and enhance overall performance, thereby increasing their market position and potential for growth.
Dynamic Technologies For A Competitive Advantage
Innovative technical amenities, such as smart recording video and podcast studios, can help provide buildings and their tenants with a competitive advantage. Equipped with advanced audio-visual technology and soundproofing, these studios allow businesses to create professional-grade content without costly off-site facilities, enhance brand presence and strengthen their market position and drive growth.
Virtual Reality And Augmented Reality Solutions
As technology advances, virtual and augmented reality solutions are becoming more accessible and relevant for workplace collaboration. By offering VR and AR capabilities within your building, an immersive experience can be created for tenants, such as virtual walk-throughs of remote sites or collaborative design sessions in a shared virtual environment. These technologies can bridge the gap between remote and in-office workers, fostering a sense of unity and camaraderie.
Access To Smart Recording Video And Podcast Studios
As businesses recognize the value of video and audio content for marketing, training and thought leadership, having access to ultramodern recording studios within the building can be a significant draw for businesses and can create a new revenue stream for building owners. Smart recording video and podcast studios, equipped with advanced audio-visual technology soundproofing and software such as Unreal Engine, allow tenants to create professional-grade content without the need for costly off-site facilities. This can help save on production costs, streamline the content creation process and enhance brand presence.
Immersive Experiences Through Green Technologies And Sustainability
Green technologies and sustainable practices can help create an immersive experience for tenants and visitors in digitally empowered buildings. By aligning with environmentally responsible practices, businesses can reduce their carbon footprint, appeal to an eco-conscious market and attract like-minded prospective tenants and their workforce.
Internet Of Things (IoT) Empowered Environmental Responsibility
Green and sustainable practices are becoming increasingly important in building design and operation. One way to achieve this is through digitally empowered buildings designed to optimize energy consumption and reduce operating costs.
Smart building systems and Internet of Things (IoT) devices can be integrated to ensure lower utility bills, efficient use of resources, and a more comfortable work environment. This not only benefits the environment but can also lead to significant savings for businesses.
Generative AI
By harnessing the power of generative AI, property managers and real estate developers can create immersive experiences tailored to individual tenant preferences, fostering a more personalized and engaging environment. Furthermore, generative AI can optimize energy consumption patterns, enabling buildings to run more efficiently and reduce their environmental impact.
By intelligently analyzing data from IoT devices and green technologies, generative AI can provide actionable insights that help drive sustainable practices in building engagement, building design and construction. This innovative fusion of generative AI with immersive and green technologies sets the stage for a truly transformative and eco-conscious property management experience, elevating tenant satisfaction and promoting responsible stewardship of the environment.
Unlocking Your Building's Full Potential
The benefits of leasing connected adaptive, dynamic and immersive buildings are substantial and can help make them the most valuable on the block. Tenants may experience more cost savings, improved collaboration, increased employee satisfaction and a competitive advantage in the market. By choosing a property that embodies these characteristics, businesses can unlock their full potential and help drive significant returns on investment.

title: Council Post: The State Of Attention: Where Is Attention-Led Advertising Going?
text:
As Chief Technology Officer and Head of Data Science, Ian Liddicoat leads the optimization of Adludio’s world-beating marketing analytics.
With digital advertising budgets under increasing scrutiny from chief revenue officers looking to streamline business costs, marketers are having to carefully consider how they measure and report back on the success of their online campaigns.
Those making the decisions on where the spend goes aren’t just interested in hearing how many views or clicks an ad received, but are demanding more quality measures of engagement, tied directly to business outcomes. This has led to an increasing desire to move away from the outdated viewability approach and toward a focus on more valuable metrics. Most notably, attention.
The attention conversation has been ongoing for some time. While there is a general acceptance that it is the future of digital ad measurement, what is still under debate is how it should be calculated.
Intelligence tells the story the eyes don’t.
Within digital media, there is a wealth of measurable behavioral data that has been harnessed to help deliver sound indicators of whether an ad has received meaningful attention.
As an example, my company’s technology can understand the relative contribution of game sequences, creative features and structural effects—such as foreground color, background color plus thousands of others—and how different combinations of these drive engagement. Other players in this space, as documented in an article in VideoWeek, are also creating technologies to help measure attention:
• Realeyes measures whether a user has been paying attention to an ad by analyzing their faces through their mobile phones’ cameras and picking up their emotional response.
• TVision utilizes sensor technology to measure both the time that an individual is in the room when TV-based content is playing and the percentage of that time in which the viewer is watching the screen.
• Adelaide makes use of ad-tracking data along with eye-tracking insights, and they have produced an attention-centered currency to replace metrics like CPM.
Moving forward, measures that focus on the quality of attention will increasingly be derived from machine learning methods, given the large volume and frequency of data involved and the need for granularity. Thanks to advances in AI, this has led to an increased level of sophistication in a number of methods such as deep learning and, ultimately, in generalized AI.
For example, techniques such as computer vision can be used to identify the structural features of an ad as well as the creative objects within it. Applying machine learning to how different combinations of creative objects deliver attention will be especially beneficial as these techniques are increasingly able to be applied in real time.
AI-based methods—including deep learning, computer vision, neural networks and natural language processing—are able to manage the relationship between all creative objects, facial recognition and text. Identifying these relationships enables advertisers to understand what contributes to meaningful attention.
Beyond just verifying whether an ad has received attention, utilizing AI in this way also enables advertisers to optimize subsequent campaigns for attention.
What’s next on the journey to capturing attention?
There are a number of approaches to attention measurement and a degree of disagreement about which elements should or should not be used.
It is necessary to consider a wide range of factors that are the direct result of meaningful or high-quality interactions from a consumer. They include, for example, hard measures such as video completion, but also video completion with sound playing. These, in turn, can be consolidated into a single model over time, and then optimized to lower funnel events, such as a completed purchase.
Moving forward, brands cannot afford to rely on subjectivity in their measurement. Instead, they must acknowledge sophisticated measures of attention based on actual consumer behavior, and how these measures drive incremental profit, increased acquisition and retention.
This will require an understanding of how consumers engage with digital content at a level of granularity not previously seen. While there are a range of AI-based techniques, brands will have to accept that AI’s assistance is essential to manage the volume and frequency of data required to measure attention.
In moving forward, both adtech companies and marketers will have to address the fears about the technology being “black box” in nature. These concerns can be increasingly addressed by working with the growing number of skilled data scientists and data engineers who understand the commercial implications of their work. Combined with the unparalleled access to many open-source libraries like PyTorch and TensorFlow, as well as cloud-based compute and memory capacity, these resources can help bring AI within the grasp of any marketer.
Conclusion
The era of attention optimization and creative intelligence is upon us. The brands that will win the battle for attention will be those who can clearly define attention metrics, optimize these through machine learning and other techniques and derive unique insights that are proven to improve customer loyalty and incremental profit.

title: Amazon Turns To AI To Drive Advertising Revenues As Overall AI Use Grows
text:
Amazon is building a new team that will work on artificial intelligence (AI) tools that generate photos and videos for merchants to use on the Amazon platform. It is a new initiative that CEO Andy Jassy approved.
What’s driving this new initiative is Amazon’s desire to build a bigger ad business. Jassy talks about Amazon looking for more sellers of the new products that have generative AI. He hopes to find new ways to place these ads across Amazon’s assortment of businesses and sees opportunities to do so in many areas, including selling sports ads on its free video streaming service as well as during Thursday night Football broadcasts on Prime video. The company also seeks to take more advantage of audio ads on Amazon Music and even run digital ads on screens inside Amazon Fresh grocery stores, among other projects.
There is an urgency for Amazon to have a strong team developing AI-supported advertising since both Meta and Google platforms, top advertising rivals, are working on similar projects according to The Information. Amazon is planning to use AI tools to find more ways for writing product descriptions as well.
I am told that e-commerce businesses like Scale AI, a relatively new startup, already promotes its generative AI products to on-line merchants. And we see that Shopify
While Jassy has cut his workforce by 27,000 co-workers, it is obvious that he wants to strengthen his existing businesses with more powerful selling tools. Advertising brought in $38 billion in revenues last year and is on track to raise revenues substantially this year.
POSTSCRIPT: We finally are learning more about how Jassy is trying to maximize the opportunities of the various businesses of Amazon. Enhancing advertising opportunities with powerful new tools will generate more income and more effectively compete with other giants. While AI is a controversial tool, it seems to be the right tool here.
More About AI. Everywhere you look these days, we see AI-based disruption in human interactions. Chatbox as a tool in customer service is not new and, as AI systems become more capable, expect to encounter more and more of them handling increasingly complex tasks. Voice synthesis and recognition technology means they will also answer the phone and even call you.
The systems will also power low-cost content generation across the web. Already they are being used as a “content farm “for news sites; one recent study found that almost 50 news websites hosted some form of obviously AI generated material but rarely labeled it as such.
What is the difference between ChatGPT, Bard, and Bing AI? All three systems are built on the same foundation, a type of AI technology called a “large language model” or LLM. But there are small differences in application that can lead to large variations in output.
ChatGPT is based on open AI’s GPT LLM, fine-tuned with a system called “reinforcement-learned human feedback” (RLHF). In giant call centers staffed by workers paid as little as $2 an hour, the company asked human trainers to rate millions of chat-style conversations with GPT in order to literally teach the AI what makes a good response and what is a bad response. However, ChatGPT cannot know the answer to questions addressing any new subject matter that emerged after its training data is set.
Microsoft
The uses of AI in these situations sound quite benign. So, why are experts linking growing use of AI to the end of humanity or society as we know it? We do not yet know what will happen if we build an AI system that is smarter than humans at everything it does.
Seemingly helpful tools can turn sinister even if well intended. A future version of ChatGPT, for instance, may prove that the best way it can help people answer questions is by slowly manipulating those very people into putting it in charge. Or, what if an authoritarian government hands too much autonomy to a battlefield robotic system letting it decide the best way to achieve its task of winning a war unrestrained by concerns for humanity.
Fears about AI ‘misuse’ already exist. Samsung bars ChatGPT at work, and Tim Cook is openly sharing his concerns about AI. The South Korean technology giant raised major alarm bells this month by banning the use of generative AI services for company work. That includes use of Open AI’s ChatGPT, Google Bard, and Microsoft’s Bing AI. Samsung grew concerned after a group of employees inadvertently uploaded company information to ChatGPT – without knowing such information would be used for training future models.
Samsung told staff it will no longer allow them to use such services on corporate devices or networks. It also discouraged using the tool on personal devices but did not outright bar them. The company even told staffers they could be fired for using the services at work, before reversing that stance. Samsung also said it is working on its own internet AI tools for summarizing documents and assisting with software development.
